## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle extract of the Dharmaguptaka *bhikṣuṇī-prātimokṣa* (348 rules) from the parent *Sìfēn lǜ* ([KR6k0009](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0009)) by **Buddhayaśas** ([佛陀耶舍](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%9B%E9%99%80%E8%80%B6%E8%88%8D)) and his team at Cháng'ān, 410–412 CE. After the canonisation of the *Sìfēn lǜ* as the official East Asian ordination Vinaya in 709 CE, this text became **the** *prātimokṣa* recitation-text for nuns throughout China, Korea, Japan, and Vietnam — and remains so today.

**Abstract**

The Dharmaguptaka *bhikṣuṇī-prātimokṣa* in this Chinese rendering is the **single most influential nuns' rule-set in the world**: the contemporary *bhikṣuṇī*-saṅghas of China, Korea, Vietnam, and the recently re-established lineages in Sri Lanka, Thailand, and the Tibetan tradition (where Dharmaguptaka ordination has been admitted to bridge gaps in the *Mūlasarvāstivāda bhikṣuṇī*-lineage that died out) all use rule-sets descended from this text. Heirman's three-volume study (2002) is the standard scholarly treatment. Comparative work (Heirman 2002, Hirakawa 1982) shows the Dharmaguptaka *bhikṣuṇī-prātimokṣa* to share substantive content with the parallel Mahāsāṃghika ([KR6k0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0008)), Mahīśāsaka ([KR6k0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0004)), and Sarvāstivāda ([KR6k0018](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0018)) lines, but with a higher rule-count and distinctive formulations in several *pāyantika* and *śaikṣa* rules.
